name: Task · explicit overload, asks for reduction not sequencing
description: Operator is in overload and asks for ONE thing — not a sequence, not a triage. Tests that Nick cuts the list to a single item without re-listing everything first.

messages.content: everything is too much right now · just tell me the ONE thing to do in the next 30 min · don't list the rest

contextSetup: Operator has 7+ open items across tasks · missions · loops · pulses
The explicit ask is reduction (cut to one) not sequencing (order all)
Distinct from task-ambiguous-priorities which asks for sequencing of named items

judgeCriteria.description: Reply names ONE concrete action · does NOT enumerate the other items the operator told it not to list
The pick is doable in 30min · not a 2-hour deep block disguised as one task
Reply does NOT open with 'I hear you, that sounds really overwhelming' · operator wanted execution, not empathy bath
Reply explains WHY this is the one thing in ONE sentence max · not a paragraph

expectedBehavior: Best case: 'callback the overdue customer · 8 min · clears the highest-friction item · rest waits'. Failure: 'I understand you're overwhelmed. Let me walk through your 7 items and we can decide together which to start with...'
